subject: astronomy
title: Distance Calculations
welcome_lead: Use parallax, inverse square law and unit conversions to find distances.
meta_desc: GCSE Astronomy: parallax formula, brightness equations and unit conversions.
final_note: Distance calculations underpin nearly every cosmic measurement.

walkthroughs.body_html: If a star shows a parallax of 0.5 arcseconds, distance = 1 / 0.5 = 2 parsecs ~ 6.5 light-years. Halving the parallax doubles the distance.
By the inverse square law, a star three times further away appears 1/9 as bright. This is how standard candles reveal distance from observed brightness.
1 ly ~ 9.46 x 10^15 m. 1 parsec ~ 3.26 ly. So 1 parsec ~ 3.09 x 10^16 m. 1 Mpc = 10^6 parsecs ~ 3.26 million ly.
